findings.title: No synopsis section found
findings.detail: Add a heading such as 'Synopsis'; reviewers skim by section and skip proposals that lack one.

findings.title: No deliverables section found
findings.detail: Add a heading such as 'Deliverable'; reviewers skim by section and skip proposals that lack one.

findings.title: No about section found
findings.detail: Add a heading such as 'About Me'; reviewers skim by section and skip proposals that lack one.

findings.title: No benefits section found
findings.detail: Most org templates ask for it; add it unless your org's template does not.

findings.title: No contributions section found
findings.detail: Most org templates ask for it; add it unless your org's template does not.

findings.title: No availability section found
findings.detail: Most org templates ask for it; add it unless your org's template does not.

findings.title: No statement about AI use
findings.detail: Check the org's AI policy; many ask you to disclose how (or whether) you used AI.

findings.title: No links to your contributions
findings.detail: Link every PR, issue, or discussion you took part in for this org; prior interaction is the strongest acceptance signal.

findings.title: No week-by-week timeline
findings.detail: Add 'Week 1', 'Week 2', ... with concrete deliverables and at least one buffer week.

findings.title: No buffer time in the timeline
findings.detail: Reviews and surprises take time; reserve some.

findings.title: No concrete references to code, files, or issues
findings.detail: Point at real files, functions, and issue numbers in the org's repository.

findings.title: 6 generic phrase(s) or buzzword(s) that read as AI-written
findings.detail: 'i am passionate about', 'cutting-edge', 'leverage', 'delve', 'in today's', 'game-changer'. Replace with specifics about this project and your own experience (https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/resources/spam_proposals).

findings.title: Short draft (47 words)
findings.detail: There is no official length, but a timeline, deliverables, and links to your work rarely fit in under 500 words. Follow the organization's template.

verdict: Not ready: fix the failures first.
manual_checks: Does it follow the organization's own template and answer every required question?
Could you explain every sentence and line of code without notes?
Did a mentor or community member see a draft before the deadline?
Is the submission on summerofcode.withgoogle.com, not only in a shared document?

checklist.title: Follow the organization's proposal template
checklist.description: Missing required sections is a common reason proposals are rejected.

checklist.title: Link prior contributions to the org
checklist.description: Link your merged pull requests, issues, reviews, or docs.

checklist.title: Show community interaction
checklist.description: Take part in the public chat or mailing list before you submit.

checklist.title: Clear scope, milestones, and weekly plan
checklist.description: Say what you will deliver each week, what is optional, and what you will cut if you fall behind.

checklist.title: Respect the org's AI policy
checklist.description: Say how you will use AI, or not, following the organization's rules.

checklist.title: Original authorship
checklist.description: Write in your own voice. You must understand every claim.

checklist.title: Submit only via the official GSoC site
checklist.description: Emailing a proposal to a mentor is not a submission.
